name: Qing Xin
parentage: Brought to Taiwan from Fujian, China.
description: 'Green Heart'. The undisputed king of Taiwanese oolongs, Qing Xin is celebrated for its ability to perfectly express the unique terroir of Taiwan's high mountains. It produces a tea with an ethereal, elegant character, a remarkably thick and creamy mouthfeel, and a delicate floral aroma of lilac and gardenia. It is the benchmark for high-end Taiwanese tea.
plantType: Relatively small, slow-growing bush that requires meticulous care and specific conditions to thrive (Camellia sinensis var. sinensis).
environment: Grows best at very high altitudes (1,000-2,600m) where cool temperatures, constant mist, and large diurnal temperature swings concentrate flavors in the leaves.
processing: Processing Qing Xin is all about preservation. The goal is to capture the pristine character of the high-mountain leaf with minimal intervention. Gentle handling and a slow, controlled withering process are essential.
oxidation: Undergoes very light oxidation (15-25%) to develop its creamy texture and floral notes without losing the freshness endowed by its high-altitude terroir.
roasting: Generally unroasted. A final, very light bake is applied for drying, but any significant roast would be seen as masking the pure, delicate character of the leaf.
versatility: Highly versatile for high-quality teas. It is the gold standard for High Mountain Oolong and Baozhong, and also makes an excellent Taiwanese green tea. Its quality ceiling is extremely high.

taiwan: Hsinchu (for Bi Luo Chun green tea)

High Mountain Oolong (Gao Shan Cha).Lishan/Alishan Oolong: Its highest expression. A lightly oxidized, unroasted, ball-rolled oolong with an incredibly thick, creamy body and delicate floral notes.

Baozhong Oolong.Pouchong: A lightly oxidized, twisted-leaf oolong that emphasizes its fresh floral aroma.

Green Tea.Sanxia Bi Luo Chun: A Taiwanese version of the famous Chinese green tea, made with this cultivar.

sensory.aroma: Elegant and ethereal Lilac, Gardenia, Cream, Fresh Mountain Air
sensory.flavor: Exceptionally smooth, buttery, and sweet with a profound and lasting aftertaste (huigan).
sensory.mouthfeel_liquor: Thick, soupy, and viscous with a very soft, creamy texture. The liquor is a pale, luminous golden-green.
